Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Salary: $70,000 - $80,000 per annum + superannuation (depending on experience and qualifications)
About Us
Community Care Services 24/7 Pty Ltd is a registered NDIS provider delivering high-quality, person-centred disability support services across the Australian Capital Territory, New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Northern Territory.
We support NDIS participants with a wide range of disabilities including intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, acquired brain injury, physical disability, and psychosocial disability. Our services include personal care, community access, domestic assistance, skills development, transportation, respite care, and support coordination.
We are committed to empowering people with disability to live their best lives, achieve their goals, and participate fully in their communities.
About the Role (Multiple positions available)
We are seeking compassionate and experienced Disability Support Workers / Aged or Disabled Carers to provide high-quality personal care and support to NDIS participants in their own homes and in community settings across Queanbeyan and surrounding areas.
This is a hands-on role providing direct care, assistance with daily living activities, emotional support, and companionship to help our participants live independently and achieve their NDIS goals.
You will work closely with participants, their families, support coordinators, and allied health professionals to deliver person-centred care in accordance with individual NDIS plans and support needs.
Key Responsibilities
Personal Care and Daily Living Support
•	Provide personal care assistance including bathing, showering, grooming, dressing, toileting and personal hygiene support
•	Assist participants with mobility, transfers, repositioning, and the use of mobility aids (wheelchairs, walkers, hoists)
•	Assist with eating and drinking, including meal preparation and feeding support where required
•	Administer medications in accordance with individual care plans and medication management protocols
•	Monitor participants' physical health and wellbeing, reporting any changes or concerns to supervisors and health professionals
Domestic Assistance
•	Perform household duties including cleaning, laundry, ironing, and general tidying
•	Prepare nutritious meals in accordance with participants' dietary requirements and preferences
•	Assist with grocery shopping and household errands
•	Maintain a clean, safe and comfortable living environment for participants
Emotional Support and Companionship
•	Provide emotional support, care and companionship to participants
•	Build positive, trusting relationships with participants and their families
•	Encourage participants' independence, dignity and self-determination
•	Support participants' mental health and emotional wellbeing through active listening and engagement
Community Access and Social Participation
•	Accompany participants to medical appointments, therapy sessions, and community activities
•	Support participants to access and participate in social, recreational, educational and vocational activities
•	Assist participants with shopping, banking, and other community-based tasks
•	Provide transportation support, including driving participants to appointments and outings
Skills Development
•	Assist participants to develop and maintain daily living skills including cooking, cleaning, budgeting, and self-care
•	Support participants to build communication, social and interpersonal skills
•	Encourage independence and capacity building in accordance with NDIS goals
•	Implement skill development programs as outlined in participants' NDIS plans
Documentation and Compliance
•	Maintain accurate progress notes, incident reports, and participant records in accordance with NDIS requirements
•	Follow individual care plans, behaviour support plans, and risk management strategies
•	Adhere to NDIS Practice Standards, Quality and Safeguarding Framework, and organisational policies
•	Report any incidents, concerns, or changes in participant needs to supervisors promptly
•	Participate in team meetings, training sessions, and professional development activities
Workplace Health and Safety
•	Follow safe manual handling techniques and use equipment correctly (hoists, lifters, mobility aids)
•	Maintain infection control practices and hygiene standards
•	Identify and report workplace hazards and risks
•	Ensure participant and personal safety at all times
Essential Requirements
Qualifications 
•	Minimum Certificate II or III 
•	OR minimum one (1) year of demonstrated relevant experience in disability support, aged care, or personal care may substitute for formal qualifications
Experience:
•	Minimum 1-3 years of relevant experience providing personal care and support to people with disabilities or aged persons
•	Demonstrated experience with personal care tasks including showering, toileting, dressing, grooming, and feeding assistance
•	Experience with medication administration and following care plans
Skills and Attributes:
•	Genuine passion for supporting people with disability to live their best lives
•	Compassionate, patient, and empathetic approach to care
•	Strong interpersonal and communication skills
•	Ability to build rapport and positive relationships with participants and families
•	Understanding of person-centred care and the NDIS framework
•	Ability to follow care plans, behaviour support plans, and support strategies
•	Physical fitness to perform manual handling tasks including lifting, transferring, and assisting with mobility
•	Reliability, punctuality, and strong work ethic
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a team
•	Flexibility to work across various shifts including mornings, afternoons, evenings, weekends, and sleepovers as required
Compliance Requirements:
•	Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (or ability to obtain prior to commencement)
•	Current Working with Vulnerable People (WWVP) Check
•	Current First Aid and CPR Certificate (HLTAID011 or equivalent)
•	Current Australian Driver's Licence and access to a reliable, comprehensively insured vehicle
•	Willingness to undergo a National Police Check
•	Legal right to work in Australia

This pivotal role goes beyond supervision; it is about providing clinical leadership, coordinating complex care, and ensuring every client receives exceptional, person-centred support that aligns with their life goals. You will be the key link between clients, their families, and a multidisciplinary care team, ensuring seamless, high-quality service delivery that promotes dignity, independence, and well-being.

Clinical Leadership & Consumer-Centred Care:
• Provide clinical leadership, supervision, and delegation to a team of care staff, offering mentorship and constructive feedback to uphold the highest standards of practice.
• Coordinate a caseload of clients with complex health and social care needs, conducting comprehensive assessments, developing tailored care plans, and evaluating interventions using evidence-based and person-centred principles.
• Act as a clinical expert, observing, reporting, and proactively responding to changes in a client’s condition, and adjusting care plans or escalating concerns appropriately.
• Provide direct, compassionate support and interventions, including emotional support and assistance with therapy plans for clients with specific needs such as dementia.

Coordination, Advocacy & Compliance:
• Liaise effectively with external healthcare providers, allied health professionals, and assessment organisations to coordinate services and ensure holistic management of each client’s needs.
• Advocate strongly for clients’ rights, including confidentiality, privacy, and supported decision-making, ensuring their voices are heard in all aspects of their care.
• Ensure strict compliance with all relevant legislation, Aged Care Quality Standards, NDIS requirements, and organisational policies, including the company's Code of Conduct.
• Lead the investigation and resolution of client incidents and feedback, participating in quality reviews and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance service delivery.

Operational Management & Safety:
• Manage client care budgets and home care agreements effectively, identifying opportunities to optimise package utilisation in line with client goals and preferences.
• Identify, assess, and document potential risks, implementing robust risk management strategies to ensure client and staff safety.
• Champion a culture of safety by adhering to and promoting all Work Health & Safety (WHS) policies, reporting hazards and near misses, and participating in safety activities.
• Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential client records within the organisation’s electronic systems, ensuring all documentation meets professional and regulatory standards.

Team & Community Engagement:
• Build and maintain strong, effective relationships with clients, their families, colleagues, and the broader community.
• Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable team environment that is responsive to client needs.
• Actively promote the organisation’s community philosophy, events, and range of services to clients and their networks.

Skills & Experience:
• A minimum of a Diploma in Aged Care, Nursing, or a relevant Allied Health field (Bachelor’s degree highly regarded).
• A minimum of one year experience in a clinical or supervisory role within aged care, community care, or a related health sector.
• In-depth understanding of Aged Care Quality Standards, Home Care Package (HCP) guidelines, and relevant compliance frameworks.
• Excellent clinical judgement, problem-solving skills, and the ability to work autonomously as a practitioner.
• Outstanding verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to adapt communication styles to diverse backgrounds.
• Strong organisational and coordination skills, with a proven ability to manage competing priorities and complex caseloads.

Mandatory Requirements:

DUTIES:

Deliver Exceptional Personal Care to Residents in Line with Individual Care Plans
• Helping residents with bathing, showering, and oral hygiene, ensuring comfort and dignity.
• Supporting dressing and grooming, respecting personal choices (e.g., preferred clothing, hairstyle).
• Assisting with toileting and continence care, using appropriate aids (e.g., pads, commodes).
• Aiding in mobility and transfers, using manual handling techniques and equipment (e.g., hoists, walkers).
• Providing meal assistance, including feeding support, modified diets (e.g., pureed foods), and monitoring hydration.
• Reviewing and adhering to individualized care plans developed by nurses or allied health professionals.
• Adjusting care approaches based on changing needs (e.g., increased support after a fall).
• Documenting care provided and noting any unmet needs or concerns for follow-up.

Support Residents’ Independence, Dignity, and Emotional Wellbeing
• Allowing residents to do tasks independently (e.g., brushing teeth, washing hands) with minimal assistance.
• Using motivational techniques (e.g., praise, encouragement) to boost confidence.
• Ensuring privacy during personal care (e.g., closing doors, using towels for coverage).
• Using respectful language (e.g., asking permission before assisting).
• Engaging in meaningful conversations to reduce loneliness.
• Recognizing signs of depression or anxiety and reporting them to supervisors.
• Facilitating social interactions (e.g., encouraging participation in group activities).

Maintain Compliance with Aged Care Standards, OH&S Policies, and Relevant Legislation
• Ensuring care aligns with dignity, choice, and quality of life principles.
• Reporting any suspected abuse or neglect as per mandatory reporting laws.
• Following infection control protocols (e.g., hand hygiene, PPE use).
• Adhering to safe manual handling to prevent resident or staff injuries.
• Identifying and reporting hazards (e.g., spills, faulty equipment).
• Maintaining confidentiality of resident information.
• Understanding consent and restraint policies (e.g., only using restraints if legally authorized).

Monitor and Report Changes in Residents’ Conditions or Concerns Regarding Care
• Noting appetite/weight loss, skin integrity (pressure sores), or mobility decline.
• Monitoring for signs of pain, infections (UTIs, wounds), or cognitive changes.
• Using electronic or paper-based systems to log observations.
• Escalating urgent concerns (e.g., sudden confusion, breathing difficulties) to nurses immediately.
• Participating in handover meetings to ensure continuity of care.

Assist with Therapy Plans, Including Dementia and Behavioural Support Interventions
• Assisting with physiotherapy exercises (e.g., walking practice).
• Encouraging participation in occupational therapy activities (e.g., puzzles, crafts).
• Using validation techniques (e.g., reassuring confused residents).
• Redirecting agitation or aggression with calming strategies (e.g., music, walks).
• Following individual behaviour support plans (BSPs) for residents with complex needs.

Foster Positive Relationships with Residents, Families, and Colleagues
• Learning their life stories, preferences, and routines for personalized care.
• Providing updates on wellbeing while respecting privacy laws.
• Addressing concerns empathetically and directing them to appropriate staff.
• Collaborating in multidisciplinary teams (nurses, therapists, cleaners).
• Resolving conflicts professionally and maintaining a positive work culture.

Participate in Workplace Safety and Continuous Improvement Initiatives
• Attending fire drills, infection control training, and manual handling refreshers.
• Reporting near-misses (e.g., a resident almost falling) to prevent future incidents.

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:
• Certificate III in Aged Care, Individual Support, or equivalent qualification.
• Minimum 1 year of full-time experience in a similar role.
• NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (issued within the last 5 years) is preferable.

• Satisfactory police check with no disclosures.
• Own reliable transportation.
• Strong teamwork skills and a commitment to long-term employment.

If you're passionate about quality aged care and meet the requirements, we'd love to hear from you!
*All successful applicants must comply with Aged Care Quality Standards and complete orientation training. *
Please submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your experience and why you'd be perfect for this role.
